chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"The 'Innin (the husband who delays consummation) is given a year, then if his wife wishes, she may marry (another), and if she wishes, she may remain."

key_terms.اَلْعِنِّينُ: A husband who delays consummating the marriage or having relations with his wife without valid excuse.
key_terms.يُتَرَبَّصُ بِهِ: He is waited for / given a period of time.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a husband who delays consummating the marriage (Innin)?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the ruling for *al-'Innin*, a husband who habitually delays consummation without valid excuse, establishing a one-year waiting period (*istibra'*) to determine if the delay is temporary or permanent. Following this year, the wife is granted the right of *khiyar* (option) to either remain in the marriage or initiate a judicial divorce (*faskh*) to marry another, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on protecting women's rights in cases of prolonged sexual neglect. This ruling underscores the principle that marriage requires mutual fulfillment of rights, and indefinite postponement by the husband constitutes grounds for the wife's release.
